:knowledge-point/_canonical-example.:knowledge-point/title: Applying the Vector Form of the Chain Rule to a Function of Two Variables

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem: If $f(x,y) = x^2 + 2 y^3$ and $\mathbf r (t) = \sin t \ \mathbf i + e^{t} \ \mathbf j,$ compute $\dfrac {\textrm d}{\textrm d t} [f(\mathbf r(t))].$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\dfrac {\textrm d}{\textrm d t} [f(\mathbf r (t))] = \nabla f(\mathbf r(t)) \cdot \mathbf r'(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $\nabla f(x,y){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+2{y}^{3})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+2{y}^{3})\,j \\  & =2x\,i+6{y}^{2}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x = \sin t$ and $y=e^{t}$  into the above to find $\nabla f(\mathbf{r}(t)){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =2(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+6({e}^{t})^{2}\,j \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+6{e}^{2t}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $\mathbf{r}(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})\,j \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+{e}^{t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\text{ }i+6{e}^{2t}\text{ }j)\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡t\text{ }i+{e}^{t}\text{ }j) \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+6{e}^{2t}\cdot {e}^{t} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡2t+6{e}^{3t}.\end{aligned}
$$

The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,j \\  & =2x\,i+2y\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x={e}^{t}$ and $y={e}^{-t}$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =2{e}^{t}\,i+2{e}^{-t}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})\,j \\  & ={e}^{t}\,i-{e}^{-t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(2{e}^{t}\,i+2{e}^{-t}\,j)\cdot ({e}^{t}\,i-{e}^{-t}\,j) \\  & =2{e}^{t}\cdot {e}^{t}-2{e}^{-t}\cdot {e}^{-t} \\  & =2{e}^{2t}-2{e}^{-2t}.\end{aligned}
$$

The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡xy)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡xy)\,j \\  & =\frac{y}{xy}\,i+\frac{x}{xy}\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{x}\,i+\frac{1}{y}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=\operatorname{cos}⁡t$ and $y={t}^{2}$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\,i+\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\,i+\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\,j)\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2t\,j) \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}+\frac{2t}{{t}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{t}-\operatorname{tan}⁡t \\  & =\frac{2-t\operatorname{tan}⁡t}{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{1+{e}^{2t}{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,i+\frac{{e}^{t}}{1+{e}^{2t}{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,j)\cdot ({e}^{t}\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{1+{e}^{2t}{sin}^{2}⁡t}+\frac{{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{1+{e}^{2t}{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}{1+{e}^{2t}{sin}^{2}⁡t}.\end{aligned}

$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3}y)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3}y)\,j \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{2}y}{{x}^{3}y}\,i+\frac{{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}y}\,j \\  & =\frac{3}{x}\,i+\frac{1}{y}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=t$ and $y={e}^{t}$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\frac{3}{t}\,i+\frac{1}{{e}^{t}}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})\,j \\  & =\,i+{e}^{t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{3}{t}\,i+\frac{1}{{e}^{t}}\,j)\cdot (\,i+{e}^{t}\,j) \\  & =\frac{3}{t}+\frac{{e}^{t}}{{e}^{t}} \\  & =\frac{3}{t}+1 \\  & =\frac{t+3}{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{xy})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{xy})\,j \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{y}}{2\sqrt{x}}\,i+\frac{\sqrt{x}}{2\sqrt{y}}\,j\text{ }\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x={t}^{3}$ and $y=t$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\frac{\sqrt{t}}{2\sqrt{{t}^{3}}}\,i+\frac{\sqrt{{t}^{3}}}{2\sqrt{t}}\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{2t}\,i+\frac{t}{2}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,j \\  & =3{t}^{2}\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{2t}\,i+\frac{t}{2}\,j)\cdot (3{t}^{2}\,i+j) \\  & =\frac{3{t}^{2}}{2t}+\frac{t}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}t+\frac{1}{2}t \\  & =2t.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
